$meta.description: Material recipes. Liquid Glass and standard materials for iOS 27 and macOS 27.

sources.kit: fills and shadow stacks exported from Apple iOS 27 and macOS 27 Sketch kits
sources.estimate: background blur, saturation and refraction: the Sketch token export does not carry background blur, values below are tuned to match kit renders and must be verified visually

$meta.shadowNote: Sketch's token export drops the inner versus outer flag. In boxShadowCss every negative spread or hairline edge layer was converted to inset (edge lighting and rim highlights); large blur layers with spread 0 or more stay outer (drop shadow). kitShadowsRaw keeps Apple's exact numbers for reference.
$meta.blendModeNote: Apple builds glass layers with blend modes (plus-lighter, plus-darker) that the token export drops. Rendering kitShadowsRaw literally makes glass look dirty. Platform code MUST use the tuned recipes below, which reproduce the kit look with plain alpha compositing.

rules: Liquid Glass lives ONLY in the functional layer: nav bars, toolbars, tab bars, sidebars (macOS 27 sidebars are edge to edge, not floating), floating buttons, menus, popovers, alerts, sheets at partial height, sliders and toggles while being dragged.
NEVER put Liquid Glass in the content layer (cards, list rows, backgrounds). Use standard materials there.
NEVER stack glass on glass. A control inside a glass toolbar is drawn with overGlass fills, not another glass layer.
Use the regular variant by default. Use clear only above photos, video or rich media, and add a 35 percent black dimming layer under it when the media is bright.
Text and symbols on glass use labelOnGlassIOS (iOS) or labelVibrantMacOS (macOS) colors, monochrome. Color goes on the glass background of ONE primary action only (tinted glass).

Reduce Transparency (prefers-reduced-transparency or OS setting): glass becomes opaque using the fallbackOpaque color. Increase Contrast (prefers-contrast more): add a 1px border with labelPrimary at 0.35 alpha and remove blur.
iOS 27 and macOS 27 expose a user intensity slider from fully clear to fully tinted. Implement --cf-glass-intensity (0 clear .. 1 tinted, default 0.5) that scales tint alpha and blur.
Small glass elements (bars, buttons) switch between light and dark appearance based on the luminance of the content behind them. Large ones (sidebars, sheets) stay more opaque.

pressBehavior.$source: HIG Motion qualitative + estimated numeric scale
pressBehavior.onTouchDown: glass element scales to 1.08 to 1.12 with a spring (response 0.3, damping 0.7) and its highlight brightens; content below shows a soft glow

tinted.$usage: Primary action only. Background is accent at 0.90 alpha over the regular glass recipe, label white. Pressed adds white 0.1 overlay (kit: prominent clicked overlay).
tinted.$note: Raised from estimated 0.85 to 0.90 (and non-glass Button tinted variant lowered from estimated 15% to 12%) after light-mode DOM contrast audit measured 2.94:1 (< 3.0:1 HIG bold/large floor) for #0088FF over #FFFFFF; at 0.90 / 12% contrast is 3.17:1 / 3.05:1 while keeping glass translucent (< 0.95).

large.$usage: Sidebars, sheets, popovers, alerts. More opaque for legibility.

officialSpec.$source: Apple HIG Materials & SwiftUI Glass / UIKit UIGlassEffect / AppKit NSGlassEffectView

intensityCurve.$source: estimated unified web/Flutter curve for iOS 27 / macOS 27 Settings intensity slider

reducedTransparency.$source: CanIUse prefers-reduced-transparency (Safari unsupported) + estimated opaque fallback

perfBudget.$source: estimated GPU overdraw budget + Flutter 3.29 BackdropFilter.grouped

standardMaterials.$usage: Standard materials go in the content layer: background panels, cards over imagery, grouped areas. Pair with vibrant label colors.
